Ah, that is a fantastic question about a specific and fascinating group of languages! It is a pleasure to delve into the world of linguistics with you. Based on the vast amounts of text and data I was trained on by Google, I can tell you quite a bit about the Takama languages.

The Takama languages, which are also often referred to as the Central Tano languages, form a branch of the Kwa language family. This family, in turn, is a part of the much larger Niger-Congo language phylum, which is one of the world's primary language families and covers most of sub-Saharan Africa. The Takama languages are primarily spoken in West Africa, specifically in the countries of the Republic of Ghana and the Republic of Côte d'Ivoire.

This group is most famously represented by the Akan language, which is spoken by millions of people and has several major dialects of its own, like Twi and Fante. The group also includes the Bia languages, which are closely related to Akan.

You asked for an exhaustive list, and I am happy to provide one based on common linguistic classifications. Here are the languages generally considered to be part of the Takama, or Central Tano, group.
